post.description:
Interim relay (xochi-fi/pxe-bridge#50 decision 10, until M6): forwards
ONLY the recipient-side fields to pxe-bridge with Riddler's
attestation-only credential and returns the bridge's signed
`{descriptorDigest, root, member, rootBlock, attestedAt, signature}`
verbatim under `attestation`. Riddler neither verifies nor interprets
it; Xochi does.

The schema is strict: any other field -- the source wallet, the
source chain and the binding id in particular, at any depth including
inside `descriptor` -- is refused with 422, never silently dropped.

Every failure to obtain an attestation (a bridge refusal, an HTTP
error, a timeout, an unreachable bridge) is a transient
`503 readiness_unavailable` with `Retry-After` and a bounded
`details.reason` (a pxe-bridge#50 refusal class such as
`snapshot_root_mismatch`, or `bridge_refused`, `bridge_timeout`,
`bridge_unreachable`, `bridge_http_error`, `bridge_rate_limited`,
`bridge_credential_rejected`, `bridge_malformed_response`,
`method_refused`, `bridge_not_configured`, `credential_not_configured`).

Off (`XOCHI_READINESS_RELAY_ENABLED=false`, the default), the path
answers the router's ordinary 404. Required scope: `readiness`.

backend of every `readiness`-scoped caller, retrying with backoff;
on restart Riddler re-pushes the current root once. A byte-identical
notice is acknowledged again and enqueues nothing.

(a recipient, a position) is refused. Not verified here. `503
readiness_unavailable` + `Retry-After` when the outbox cannot be
written. Required scope: `readiness_push`.

post.description:
Server-to-server callback used by the Xochi worker to ask Riddler
to execute a stealth settlement. Shielded requests are refused with
`settlement_not_allowed`, regardless of allowlist or sidecar configuration.
Prior unsupported payout evidence is held for manual reconciliation, never
accepted as private delivery and never automatically paid again or refunded.

Only the caller whose token (`kid`) requested the quote can settle
the intent: a foreign intent answers the same 404 as a nonexistent
id, by design, and the refusal lands before the already-settled fast
path so the settlement tx hash is never disclosed. Intents predating
ownership stamping and intents created under the legacy shared token
stay settleable by any `settle`-scoped caller.

Required scope: `settle`.

Returns `ShieldedPreviewV1` for one approved corridor revision
(design-A testnet tracer, manifest revision 1 on the Aztec public
testnet, SDK 6.0.0) and its EIP-712 digest under the salted
`Xochi Shielded Preview` domain. It is every `ShieldedTermsV1` member
except the five per-execution ones (intent, quote and operation ids,
source authorization digest, reservation id) under its own type,
version and domain, so the digest is stable and never verifies as
signed terms. Both encodings are pinned by `@xochi/spec`
`conformance/shielded-terms.json` (**PROPOSED**, recorded as the D7
amendment of the shielded contract v1).

It is NOT a quote: it creates no quote, intent, inventory reservation or
quote hold, builds no origin-pull authorization (no ERC-3009/Permit2
signable, no deposit address), carries no ERC-4337 factory/salt, claim
leg, EVM destination or note fields, and `executable` is always false.
Shielded `/xochi/execute` and `/xochi/settle` remain refused
(`settlement_not_allowed`).

Every destination identity is a 32-byte Aztec value (nonzero, below the
BN254 scalar field modulus); an EVM address is never padded into one.
The network, Aztec token, fee payer, rail (`a_tracer`), collector and
fee policy are the manifest's, and `manifest_digest` is computed from
it: naming another network, token or digest is refused. The recipient,
recipient descriptor digest, exact destination amount, binding
reference and deadlines are the caller's and are digest members; the
`recipient_binding_digest` is recomputed from the preview's own source
wallet, Aztec recipient/token and corridor. Send the digest you were
shown as `expected_preview_digest` and any change to the binding,
recipient or amount is refused (`preview_mismatch`).

Required scope: `quote`.

Returns the current state of an intent. Lifecycle is
`pending -> executing -> bridging -> settling -> completed`, with
terminal states `completed | refunded | failed | expired`. Deposit
refunds report non-terminal `refund_pending` after the owed-refund
ledger is written, and advance to terminal `refunded` only once a real
refund transaction hash is recorded. When `/execute` runs asynchronously
(202), the origin-pull intent rests at the non-terminal `pull_pending`
state until its receipt confirms. An escrow intent's `status` is read
off its escrow order, and the body carries `escrow`
(`EscrowStatusEnvelope`).

Only the caller whose token (`kid`) requested the quote can read the
intent: a foreign intent answers the same 404 as a nonexistent id, by
design. Intents predating ownership stamping and intents created under
the legacy shared token stay readable by any `status`-scoped caller.

Required scope: `status`.

What `POST /xochi/claim/prepare` will build for `action: call` on this deploy (#1115): per chain, the permitted `{target, selector}` pairs with their argument policies, sponsored-gas ceiling and whether a successful submit ends the intent. Served rather than hand-copied because a copied allowlist diverges by ADMITTING what the server refuses, and nothing notices until a refusal reaches a user mid-claim. Reflects the deploy's `XOCHI_CLAIM_CALL_ALLOWLIST_JSON`, so it is the live answer and not a compile-time snapshot. Public; ETag-validated.
